passage_ledger.name: Passage Ledger
passage_ledger.description: Five bays in a row, 3.59 m end to end, each holding the SAME axis_translation_cube body at the SAME instant of the SAME motion and differing only in what account the artifact gives of that motion. The five are the source's own ACCOUNTS list read at build time, not retyped: ghost keeps the guide rail, the green and red end markers and a four-instance trail; sweep replaces the history with one wireframe bar the full length of the travel, the cube inside it like a capital on a column; terminus throws away the middle and pins two solid cubes at the two extremes; formula gives up the picture and states the rule on a plate; none keeps the result and admits nothing. The cube, the rail, the bar, the termini and the plate are the source's geometry at 1:1 built by the source's arithmetic from cube_size 0.15, travel_distance r and travel_speed 0.3, in the swept token's own blue (0.3, 0.6, 1.0). What the axes turn is not the account - that is EXHIBITED across the row - but WHEN you looked and HOW FAR the passage goes. `state` is the source FSM's four instants; `reach` is travel_distance at three of its own landmarks. Both moving instants pin the cube at offset 0.000 with the same colour and the same emission, so those two frames are identical everywhere except the trail, and the only thing in the ledger that knows which way the object is going is the one deposit the runtime has never actually drawn.
dev_themes: five theories of what a still can hold of a motion
the account named for holding history holds none at rest
the ghost the runtime has never drawn
writing the rule out takes four times the room that doing it takes
interactions: read the row left to right at moving_positive/stride - one passage told five ways, the cube identical in all five bays and everything around it different
step to wait_positive and watch bay 3's live cube DISAPPEAR into its own terminus claim: at that instant the two are the same transform, which is the only moment terminus is true
walk to reach=nudge and watch bay 0's trail retreat inside its own cube while bay 4 does not change by one pixel - below a certain reach nothing in the ledger records the passage at all
compare the two moving instants at any reach: everything is identical except three ghosts mirrored about the datum and four glyphs of direction word
passage_ledger.capacity: SEE that a still frame cannot hold a motion, only what the motion DEPOSITS, and that the deposit is a choice with consequences. Read left to right the row is a subtraction: ghost keeps everything and shows a hairline; sweep trades the history for the orbit and gains a body; terminus throws away the middle and gains the two instants when its own claim is exactly true; formula gives up the picture and is the only bay a still can hold COMPLETELY; none keeps the result and admits nothing. SEE ALSO what the proportions say without a label: the pitch of the whole row is set by the one bay whose content is TEXT, because the formula plate is 0.57-0.76 m wide against a 0.15 m cube. And see the failure the family did not intend - the account NAMED for holding history holds none whenever the object is at rest, at every reach, which is most of the time.
passage_ledger.qfep_connection: F is the deposit - whatever survives the motion into the frame, and every bay commits to a different one. E is the passage itself, which is IRREDUCIBLE to any of them: the cube crossing its own base_position is the same event in all five bays and no bay contains it. lambda is what each account is willing to spend to say so - one bar, two cubes, four ghosts, two lines of ASCII, or nothing. The dark spot is `none`, and it is not empty. _setup_controls runs unconditionally and BEFORE _build_account, so `none` withholds the operation and keeps the apparatus: a cube, a cream control panel, and an invisible 0.95 m anchor. What is foreclosed by this ledger is the motion itself - twelve tiles and not one of them moves, which is the law being obeyed and the subject being lost in the same gesture. What is bought is the only reading a still permits: five epistemologies of evidence, side by side, at one scale, which no single member's room could ever show.
passage_ledger.relationships:
Synthesised out of ONE family with four names. [[axis_translation_cube]] and its three siblings [[x_translation_cube]], [[y_translation_cube]] and [[z_translation_cube]] are the SAME script and the same scene folder (commons/artifacts/axis_translation_cube/), differing only in `axis`, `course` and `cube_color` - the corpus's one-scene-many-names pattern, and all four declare the same two axes in commons/artifacts/registry/transforms.json.

WORDS TAKEN, NOT MINTED (LAW 13). The five bays ARE axis_translation_cube.gd:96 `const ACCOUNTS: PackedStringArray = ["ghost", "sweep", "terminus", "formula", "none"]`, and passage_ledger.gd:725 iterates that const rather than a copy of it, so a rename in the source renames a bay here. `state` is axis_translation_cube.gd:24 `enum State { MOVING_POSITIVE, WAIT_POSITIVE, MOVING_NEGATIVE, WAIT_NEGATIVE }` lowercased in enum order, cross-checked against SRC.State at run time (gd:489-499). `reach` is the only coinage, and its three values are travel_distance's own landmarks rather than taste.

WAVE KIN: [[ghost_court]], the other synthesis in this wave, whose `complement` axis is [none, ghost, supply, redaction, quorum]. The two families coined `ghost` and `none` independently. See dna.ghost_meaning for what they mean HERE, derived from the code, so the two can be set side by side.

CONSTRUCTION KIN, and a deliberate refusal of the last two waves' form: [[pressure_yard]] and [[ladder_hall]] both reduced their families to an order-statistic rack - identical slats on grey pads - and pressure_yard recorded the fault in its own registry while the next wave repeated it. This ledger has NO rack, NO slat, NO pad, NO plinth, NO shared scale bar and NO bar-chart-in-3D anywhere. Every bay carries the source's own body at 1:1 in the source's own palette. The nearest right-shaped precedents are [[tier_terrarium]] (organisms in bays) and [[boundary_tank]] (four actual standing waves).

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE WIDTH IS THE CONSTRAINT AND THE DEPTH IS ALMOST NOTHING. The mesh row is 3.590 x 0.950 x 0.218 m, four cells by one, and it stands from y = 0.000 (the bottom of the longest run, by construction: BASE_Y is STRIDE_M + CUBE_SIZE * 0.5 so the deepest offset lands exactly on the floor) to y = 0.950. The Label3D block goes higher - the name plates sit at y = 1.236 with a half-height near 0.058 - so the OCCUPIED height is about 1.294 m, two cells, even though the AABB the capture rig measures stops at 0.950 (capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D only, and a Label3D is not one). front 4 because a 3.59 m row wants the reader far enough back to hold five bays at once and the whole argument is the COMPARISON; back 0 because the deepest thing in the row is the datum rod at z -0.143 and the shallowest the formula plate at z +0.18. left/right 1 because the outermost lit mark is bay 0's readout, which reaches 0.225 m past the outermost cube.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - not a Godot measurement pass. The row is authored so that ONE layers = 0 MeshInstance3D anchor (gd:736-746) IS the union AABB, and passage_ledger.gd:533-551 asserts every number in it at run time: ROW_W = 4 * BAY_PITCH + CUBE_SIZE = 3.590, ROW_H = 2 * STRIDE_M + CUBE_SIZE = 0.950, ROW_D = 0.075 - (-0.143) = 0.218, centre z = -0.034, radius = 1.859981. VERIFIED HERE BOX BY BOX rather than trusted: every vertex of every mesh at all twelve variants lies inside that box, the worst case being reach = nudge, whose own geometry spans only (-1.795, 0.350, -0.143) to (1.795, 0.600, 0.075). The anchor is required twice over - `reach` swings the row's real vertical extent by 3.8x (0.95 m at stride to 0.25 m at nudge), which without it would make the sheet a picture of a zoom, and bay 0's trail is a MultiMeshInstance3D, which _subtree_aabb ignores whenever any MeshInstance3D exists. Re-measure when a Godot pass is run.

dna.default:
state=moving_positive, reach=stride.

BOTH ARE THE CODE'S OWN @export DEFAULTS, read off passage_ledger.gd:320 and :327 and not chosen here. dna.placements is 0 - verified this pass by grepping every JSON under commons/ for the token, which returns only ghost_court.json's kin reference and no map_data.json - so the defaults had only to be the strongest single readings, and they already were.

state=moving_positive is the FSM's own first member (axis_translation_cube.gd:24 State.MOVING_POSITIVE, and gd:117 `var _state: State = State.MOVING_POSITIVE`), and it is also the instant that makes the sheet legible: at a moving state the cube stands at offset 0.000 on the datum, so the five bays line up on one horizontal and the accounts are read against a common baseline. Opening on a wait state would open with the cube parked on top of one end marker, swallowing it.

reach=stride is travel_distance's shipped default (axis_translation_cube.gd:31) and every frame this family has ever produced. It is also the only value at which `ghost` shows three ghosts - see dna.predicted_relationship for the census - so it is the value at which the bay named for history actually has some.
dna.was: nothing. This token did not exist before this pass and neither did the arrangement. Measured, not assumed: axis_translation_cube declares `account` with five values and every one of them has only ever been photographed ALONE, one variant per tile, so the five accounts of one passage have never stood in a single frame. The four member scenes carry no non-default placement anywhere in the corpus.
dna.note:
WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY DECLARES, read out of the code for this entry rather than transcribed (LAW 2).

axis_translation_cube.gd:66  @export_enum("lateral", "lift", "depth") var course: String = "lift"
axis_translation_cube.gd:95  @export_enum("ghost", "sweep", "terminus", "formula", "none") var account: String = "ghost"

with `const COURSES` at :67 and `const ACCOUNTS` at :96 beside them, and _read_dna (:139-162) gating on `.has()`. Both are genuine engine-enforced hints, so tools/check_dna_declarations.py has a hint_string to read there - unlike the four benches ladder_hall was built out of, which that entry records as declaring their axis with a plain typed String and a trailing comment.

THIS SYNTHESIS DECLARES NEITHER OF THOSE. It declares `state` and `reach`, both real @export_enum (passage_ledger.gd:320 and :327), and it EXHIBITS `account` as the five bays. That is the whole shape of the artifact: the axis the family argues with is laid out in space so a still can hold all five at once, and the two axes that are swept are the two the family never named - WHEN you looked, and HOW FAR the passage goes.

WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM, and every one is asserted at run time against a live orphan instance of the source (gd:404-457, _probe_source, which calls SRC.new(), reads cube_size / travel_speed / wait_time / travel_distance / trail_count / cube_color / show_rail / show_trail and the export's own range minimum out of get_property_list(), asks the FSM for each of its four direction words with the assignment READ BACK, and then frees it):
  stride 0.40  travel_distance's shipped default (:31)
  body   0.15  exactly cube_size (:29) - the passage is one object long
  nudge  0.05  the @export_range's own MINIMUM (:31) - one third of a body

CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD. The code wins in all six; four of them correct this artifact's OWN header.

 1. THE SWEEP CAP IS 16, NOT 9. passage_ledger.gd:296-297 says "build_dna_gallery --max DEFAULTS TO 9 and must be run with --max=12 or three tiles vanish silently". tools/build_dna_gallery.py:136 is `cap = 16`, and the comment at :127 explains why it was raised. 4 x 3 = 12 fits at the default and NOTHING is trimmed. The header is stale. The operational ruling survives it: never run this sweep below --max=12, because the trim eats the END of the LATER axis and at cap 9 `reach` goes from three values to two, dropping `nudge` - which is the value dna.predicted_degeneracy is entirely about.

 2. THE HEADER'S PIXEL FIGURES FOR LONG VERTICAL RUNS OMIT THE VERTICAL FORESHORTENING. The camera's up vector is (-0.149373, 0.966390, -0.209232), so a world-vertical metre projects to 0.966390 m of screen. The header's "travel run 161.2 px" is 0.95 m x 169.7 px/m with that factor left out; the rail measures 156.3 px and the actual 0.8 m of travel 131.7 px at bay 0. Every horizontal figure and every small mark in that header reproduces to within a pixel - cube edge 25.5 against 25.6 measured, marker sphere 6.8 against 6.8, rail diameter 2.7 against 2.7, formula em 14.9 against 15.0 - so the error is confined to the tall runs.

 3. THE BAY DEPTHS ARE 0.027 M NEARER THAN THE HEADER SAYS. It quotes 7.323 / 6.840 / 6.357 / 5.875 / 5.392, which is the distance to the row's centre LINE; the rig aims at the union AABB centre, which sits at z = -0.034, 0.027 m behind it along the view axis. Measured: 7.2965 / 6.8136 / 6.3308 / 5.8479 / 5.3650. The gauge moves 0.4% (169.7 -> 170.3 px/m at the worst bay) and nothing in the argument turns on it.

 4. THE COINCIDENCE AT THE WAIT STATES IS DETERMINISTIC, BUT NOT BY THE MECHANISM THE HEADER NAMES. gd:227-228 says "It is made deterministic by draw order: the live cube is the last opaque body added to its bay". GDScript child order does not decide Godot's opaque draw order - opaque geometry is sorted by material and shader, not by tree index - and the depth comparison is LESS, so at exactly equal depth whichever draw arrives SECOND is rejected, whichever that is. The conclusion holds and the sheet is safe, but for a different reason: the same two materials (a StandardMaterial3D terminus cube and a Grid.gdshader live cube) meet in exactly the same way in every tile that has the coincidence, so whichever wins wins in all of them, and the comparison is unaffected. It is not a fudge and it is not a z-fight in the flicker sense; it is one surface decided by the renderer's own sort.

 5. transforms.json declares `course` as ["lift", "lateral", "depth"] while axis_translation_cube.gd:67 declares ["lateral", "lift", "depth"]. Registry and code agree as a SET and disagree as a SEQUENCE, which matters because build_dna_gallery trims from the END. Not this file's business to edit and not this artifact's axis, but it is the kind of drift that silently reorders a sibling's tiles.

 6. `none` IS NOT EMPTY, AND THE SOURCE'S OWN MEASUREMENT BLOCK PROVES IT INDEPENDENTLY. _setup_controls (:129, :354-366) is called unconditionally and BEFORE _build_account, so the cream RackTemplates panel titled "TRANSLATION" stands 0.6 m in front of the cube at every account value including `none`, and _add_travel_anchor (:671-687) leaves a 0.95 m invisible box behind. Confirmation from outside the script: transforms.json records axis_translation_cube's measured aabb_size as [0.29, 0.96, 0.64] with centre z 0.32 - two thirds of that measured DEPTH is the control panel. See dna.declines for why this ledger omits it anyway and what that omission costs.
dna.ghost_meaning:
WHAT `ghost` AND `none` MEAN IN THIS FAMILY, DERIVED FROM axis_translation_cube.gd. Stated flat so it can be set beside ghost_court's `complement` axis word for word.

GHOST IS NOT A TRAIL. IT IS THE UN-SUBTRACTED WHOLE. _read_dna's match (:153-162) sends "sweep", "terminus", "formula" to one branch and "none" to another; "ghost" falls through to a bare `pass` at :161-162, so all three want-flags stay true. _build_account (:568-579) then adds nothing for it either - :578-579 is a second bare `pass`. There is no code anywhere in the file that runs BECAUSE the value is ghost. What makes a frame "ghost" is purely that NOTHING WAS CLEARED: the legacy build survives entire - rail, two end markers, three labels, a four-instance MultiMesh. It is a DEFAULT wearing a name.

AND THE THING IT IS NAMED FOR HAS NEVER BEEN VISIBLE, IN ANY STILL OR IN ANY MOTION. _trail_history[0] is the cube's CURRENT offset (:453) and the array shifts ONE SLOT PER RENDERED FRAME (:451-452), so the four samples lag by 0, 1, 2 and 3 frames - 0, 5, 10 and 15 mm at 60 fps and at the shipped travel_speed of 0.3 m/s - while their half-extents are 37.5, 43.1, 48.8 and 54.4 mm against the cube's 75 mm. Grid.gdshader writes no ALPHA and declares no blend mode (:2-3, :79-80), so the cube is fully opaque and swallows all four. The visibility condition is i * step > 0.075 * (1 + scale_i), binding at i = 1: step > 0.118125 m, i.e. travel_speed / fps > 0.118125, i.e. FPS <= 2.54. THE TRAIL IS VISIBLE ONLY BELOW 2.54 FRAMES PER SECOND. Worse than discarded: Grid.gdshader:59-65 selects instanceColor as the BASE colour whenever its alpha is under 0.99, and every trail instance is 0.25 or less, so a ghost that did clear the cube would render at full (0.3, 0.6, 1.0) - flat, with no wireframe at all, because wireframeColor carries the same rgb - which is BRIGHTER than the cube's own (0.06, 0.12, 0.20) interior. The faintest ghost would be the most luminous body in the bay.

So in this family GHOST means: everything, minus nothing - including the one part of itself nobody has ever seen. The value named ghost is a ghost of a ghost.

NONE IS THE ONLY VALUE THAT CLEARS THE LABELS AS WELL AS THE RAIL AND THE TRAIL (:157-160), and like ghost it ADDS nothing (:576-577 is a third bare `pass`). So the two words are the SAME BUILDER BRANCH - a `pass` - separated only by what was cleared before it ran: one clears nothing, the other clears everything. But `none` is not empty and never has been. _setup_controls (:129, :354-366) runs unconditionally and BEFORE _build_account, so the cream RackTemplates panel titled "TRANSLATION" stands 0.6 m in front of the cube in `none` exactly as in the other four, and _add_travel_anchor leaves a 0.95 m invisible box behind it. `none` is the result plus its instrument plus its frame: the OPERATION is withheld, the APPARATUS is not.

THE WAVE QUESTION, ANSWERED FROM THIS SIDE. Neither word describes a picture here. Both name an operation on a BUILD. If the other family's `ghost` means "a translucent copy of a former state", the two do NOT agree, and this family is the one that breaks: here ghost is a default, its copies are OPAQUE, they GROW with age rather than fade (0.500 newest to 0.725 oldest, :457), they are enclosed inside the object, and they have never been rendered. On `none` the two agree only halfway - both use it for withholding - and this family adds the finding the other cannot: withholding the account does not withhold the apparatus. Measured on this sheet, `none` is the value that reads ZERO under BOTH axes at the two moving instants (nine exact zeros, dna.predicted_degeneracy) and non-zero under `reach` at the two wait instants. It is silent about DIRECTION always, and silent about DISTANCE only while the object is between the ends.
dna.kin:
THE FIVE BAY WORDS ARE TAKEN CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER AND ARE NOT RETYPED (LAW 13). passage_ledger.gd:305 preloads axis_translation_cube.gd and :405 assigns `_accounts = SRC.ACCOUNTS`; _build (:725-726) iterates that const, so the bays ARE the source's list and a rename in the source renames a bay here. gd:502-504 pushes an error if the list ever stops having five members. This is the stronger form ladder_hall's own entry named as its weakness - that hall retyped its five strings and would have kept declaring a stale one.

`state` IS THE FAMILY'S OWN LIST TOO, and it is checked in both directions. It is axis_translation_cube.gd:24 `enum State { MOVING_POSITIVE, WAIT_POSITIVE, MOVING_NEGATIVE, WAIT_NEGATIVE }`, lowercased, in enum order. gd:489-499 reads SRC.State back at run time and errors on any member that disagrees by position; gd:506-527 reads this file's own @export hint string out of get_property_list() and compares it to the const in BOTH directions AND in order. An @export_enum literal cannot be built from a const at parse time, so reading the hint back is the only defence against the science_screen failure - a hand-typed block declaring none|bezel|hooded|cabinet against a code enum of stand|wall|console|rig, where the sweep set an invalid value, the artifact fell back to its default, sixteen identical frames were published and the critic reported the axis INERT at 0.69%.

`state` IS UNUSED AS AN AXIS NAME ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE CORPUS, so nothing collides.

`reach` IS THE ONE COINAGE, and its three values are landmarks rather than taste: the shipped default, exactly one cube_size, and the export range's own minimum. It is named for what the number MEANS to a standing body - how far the passage goes, in units of the thing that goes - on the same principle as the source's own `course`, which is named lateral/lift/depth rather than X/Y/Z.

`phase` WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED. traverse|crest|steepest|trough is the nearest neighbours' word for the same question - y_oscillation_cube, velocity_arrow, slope_tangent_demo, partial_derivative_terrain - but this motion is piecewise LINEAR at 0.3 m/s and has no steepest point and no crest, so importing that list would ship a designed twin with no referent. `state` is the family's own vocabulary for the same axis and it has four real members.

WAVE KIN. ghost_court declares `complement` = [none, ghost, supply, redaction, quorum]. `ghost` and `none` are shared with this family and were coined independently on both sides. dna.ghost_meaning states what they mean here, from the code, so the comparison can be made rather than assumed.
dna.declines:
`account` REFUSED AS AN AXIS, AND THIS IS THE DESIGN. It is the family's loudest knob and it is right there, five values, engine-enforced. Sweeping it would produce five tiles of five different objects and would answer the question the family already answers on its own bench. EXHIBITING it puts all five in ONE frame at one scale under one light, which is the only thing a synthesis can do that a sweep of the member cannot. The consequence is declared and is checked at run time: because `account` is exhibited, all twelve tiles carry the IDENTICAL node census - 13 MeshInstance3D, 1 MultiMeshInstance3D of 4 instances, 14 Label3D - and gd:587-590 pushes an error if that ever stops being true.

`course` REFUSED AND PINNED TO "lift", AND THE REFUSAL IS MEASURED, NOT TASTE (LAW 13 asks for the family's list; this declines two thirds of it on the record). Two reasons. (1) THE ROW IS A ROW. At `lateral` the 0.95 m run lies along the row axis, the widest tenant's screen-x half-extent rises from 0.183 to 0.430 m, LAW 9 then demands a pitch of at least 1.18 m, the union AABB goes from 3.59 to 5.67 m and every mark in the sheet loses 36% - the formula plate's em falls from 15.0 px to 9.8 px, and the bay whose entire body is text has to be readable or LAW 1 fails there. (2) THE CRITIC'S CROP IS NON-UNIFORM. artifact_dna_critic crops to the union subject box and resizes to 160 x 160 whatever its shape; this row crops 625 x 262, squashing horizontal detail 3.91x and vertical only 1.64x, so `lift` puts the whole state axis on the better-preserved screen axis. It is worth about 2.4x on the measurement.

AND THE PIN COSTS A COLOUR, WHICH IS ALSO ON THE RECORD. axis_translation_cube.tscn overrides nothing, so cube_color is the script default (0.3, 0.6, 1.0) and this ledger is blue. But the sibling scene that actually carries course = "lift" - y_translation_cube.tscn - overrides cube_color to (0.3, 0.8, 0.4), GREEN. The ledger is the SWEPT token's blue because the swept token is the one that declares the axes; a viewer who has met the lift member in a map has met it green.

EVERY RATE, EVERY DURATION AND EVERY ANIMATION REFUSED (LAW 5). The source is nothing BUT a rate: _process runs five updaters every frame (:373-378). This file has no _process, no Timer, no await, no signal, no tween and no clock read anywhere; _ready (:387-394) runs six synchronous calls and stops. The FSM is instead run BACKWARDS in closed form - _pinned_offset (:622-627) reproduces the source's own clamps at :386 and :398 exactly, and _trail_history (:665-672) spatialises the history at a step of travel_distance / (trail_count - 1), which is not a taste but THE ONLY step for which the four samples are a complete record of the current half-run: three steps back is exactly r / 0.3 seconds, exactly r metres, exactly the instant the run began.

NO RANDOMNESS, SO NO SEED IS DECLARED (LAW 6). Neither file contains randf, randi, randomize or RandomNumberGenerator. Every position in the ledger is arithmetic over CUBE_SIZE, STRIDE_M, BODY_M, NUDGE_M, TRAVEL_SPEED, WAIT_TIME, TRAIL_COUNT and BAY_PITCH. There is nothing for a seed export to pin.

THE VR SPEED SLIDER REFUSED. _setup_controls builds a RackTemplates panel with a live SPEED slider (:354-366). A slider is a rate by definition and a still cannot hold it; and the panel itself is omitted for the reason in dna.still_note.

A SIXTH BAY REFUSED. The obvious extension is a bay for the account the family does NOT have - the motion itself, an arrow or a streak. That would be a symbol of a passage rather than a deposit of one, and the whole argument is that a still holds deposits only.

FULL-HEIGHT DIVIDERS AND ANY SHARED SCALE BAR REFUSED. The measured daylight between adjacent bay marks is 41.5 px at its worst (terminus to formula), and a divider that reads at LAW 8's 10 px floor with 10 px of air either side would eat 30 of it, forcing the pitch past 1.15 m and the row past 4.75 m. More to the point, a shared gauge is the rack form this wave exists to refuse: the bays are meant to be incommensurable, because that is the finding.
dna.framing_why:
0.55, AND IT IS THE CODE'S NUMBER, NOT THIS ENTRY'S. passage_ledger.gd:542 computes `radius / tan(deg_to_rad(17.0)) * 1.9 * 0.55` and asserts the result equals 6.3575 (gd:543). A registry that declared anything else would put the artifact's own self-check at odds with the rig.

THE UNION AABB IS AN AUTHORED BOX, NOT AN EMERGENT SUM. One layers = 0 MeshInstance3D anchor (gd:736-746) is sized (3.590, 0.950, 0.218) at centre (0, 0.475, -0.034), and it is the union at all twelve variants - verified box by box in an independent Python replica: every vertex of every mesh at every variant lies inside it, the worst case being reach = nudge, whose own geometry spans only (-1.795, 0.350, -0.143) to (1.795, 0.600, 0.075). Diagonal 3.719963, radius 1.859981.

THE RIG: dist = 1.859981 / tan(17 deg) * 1.9 * 0.55 = 6.357493 m, so the visible half-frame at the row centre is 1.943681 m. Camera basis reproduced to six places: right (0.813878, 0, -0.581035), up (-0.149373, 0.966390, -0.209232), view direction (0.561507, 0.257081, 0.786524). +X therefore reads LEFT TO RIGHT on screen, so the row reads in the ACCOUNTS order, and +Z projects screen-LEFT, which is why the formula plate at z = +0.18 overhangs toward terminus rather than toward none.

WHY 0.55 AND NOT 1.0. The rig fits by the bounding SPHERE and this row is 16.5x wider than it is deep, so at framing 1.0 the whole subject falls to 338 px of 760 - 44.5% of frame width - and more than half the frame is empty. Measured at each candidate, projecting every mesh vertex and every label quad at all twelve variants:

  framing   dist m    subject screen-x span      width      verdict
  0.50      5.7795    [  81.9, 785.0]            703 px     CLIPS the right edge by 25 px
  0.52      6.0107    [  91.9, 765.2]            673 px     CLIPS by 5 px
  0.55      6.3575    [ 105.7, 739.0]            633 px     fits, 21 px of right margin
  0.60      6.9354    [ 125.9, 702.4]            577 px     fits, every mark 8.3% smaller
  1.00     11.5591    [ 220.2, 558.1]            338 px     44.5% of width, half the frame wasted

0.55 IS THE TIGHTEST VALUE THAT DOES NOT CLIP, AND THE MARGIN IS 21 PX ON THE RIGHT. The frame is deliberately asymmetric: the left margin is 105.7 px and the right 21.0 px, because +Z projects screen-left while bay 4 is the NEAREST bay, so the near end of the row swings right. FIVE CLAIMS, ALL FALSIFIABLE, ALL STATED BEFORE ANY GODOT RENDER EXISTS.

(1) THE DECOMPOSITION, AND IT IS THE THESIS. At any fixed reach, moving_positive and moving_negative are IDENTICAL everywhere except in two places. _pinned_offset (:622-627) puts the cube at offset 0.000 at BOTH moving values, so the lerp parameter is t = (0/r + 1)/2 = 0.5 in both, and _update_color_feedback reproduced at :697-708 gives both the same wireframe colour (0.315, 0.645, 0.910), the same emission x1.5 and the same emission_strength 0.7. The sweep bar, the two terminus cubes, the formula plate, the datum, the rail, the two end markers, all five name plates and the first line of every readout are therefore byte-identical across such a pair. Exactly two things are not: bay 0's trail, mirrored about the datum, and four glyph-blocks of direction word - "up" against "down" in the readouts of bays 0 to 3, because _get_direction_name (:429-443) is the only thing in the whole ledger that knows the sign. FALSIFYING TEST, checkable on any bay crop: at a fixed reach, the sweep, terminus and formula bays must differ between the two moving states ONLY in the readout's second line. Measured on the replica they differ by 0.0439 / 0.0526 / 0.0459 percent at stride and 0.0442 / 0.0544 / 0.0425 at nudge - FLAT to three decimals across a 8x change in reach, which is the signature of a text-only difference. If any of those six cells moves with reach, something other than the word is changing and claim 3 is void.

(2) THE GHOST CENSUS, WHICH IS THE DECLARED CROSSING BETWEEN THE TWO AXES. `reach` moves the cube only at the two WAIT states; the trail exists only at the two MOVING states. The axes are independent in construction and interacting in effect, and `reach` is exactly what decides whether a ghost is visible at all: ghost i clears the opaque cube iff i * r / 3 > 0.075 * (1 + 0.5 + i * 0.075), i.e. r > 0.354375 at i = 1, 0.185625 at i = 2 and 0.129375 at i = 3. So stride shows THREE ghosts, body shows ONE and nudge shows NONE. _check_ghost_census (:557-584) asserts that table at run time and independently reproduces here. The partial protrusions are the finer statement and they are what the pixels actually see: protrusion = |lag| + half_i - 0.075 gives +0.1015 / +0.2404 / +0.3794 m at stride, +0.0181 / +0.0737 / +0.1294 at body and -0.0152 / +0.0071 / +0.0294 at nudge. FALSIFIED IF a nudge tile shows a ghost standing clear of its cube, or a stride tile shows fewer than three.

(3) THE SATURATION, AND IT IS THE ARTIFACT'S TRUTH LINE. At BOTH wait states, at EVERY reach, the trail holds nothing: the FSM's own clamp has pinned the offset for wait_time seconds, so three of the four samples are the identical clamped value and the fourth is 0.100 m back at stride, under the 0.129375 m it would need to clear the cube. The account named for holding history holds none whenever the object is at rest, which is 2 of every 7.333 seconds at stride and 2 of every 3.0 at nudge. gd:573-584 pushes an error if that ever stops being true. FALSIFIED IF any wait tile shows a ghost.

(4) THE NINE EXACT ZEROS, all on bay 4's crop, all checkable independently of any threshold. `none` holds a cube and a name plate and nothing else, and at a moving state that cube stands at offset 0.000 whatever `reach` says. So bay 4 must be PIXEL-IDENTICAL (a) between the two moving states at each of the three reaches, and (b) across all three reach pairs at each of the two moving states. Measured on the replica: 0 sum and 0 pixels in all nine. THE MIRROR MUST NOT BE ZERO: at the two WAIT states the cube stands at +/-r, so bay 4 across reach measures 0.97% to 1.41% on its own crop. Any non-zero in the nine means the rig is not deterministic and voids the whole pass; any zero in the six wait-state cells means the sweep never set `reach`, and <out>/_rejects.json is the first thing to read.

(5) THE AXIS VERDICTS, PRE-REGISTERED so the critic cannot be read charitably afterwards. In the critic's own currency the replica gives `state` a mean of 1.6084% frame / 28.7290% focus over its 18 pairs and `reach` a mean of 3.7995% / 53.6441% over its 12. Against artifact_dna_critic's thresholds (INERT_FOCUS 0.030, WEAK_FOCUS 0.120, WEAK frame 0.020), `reach` lands on BITES outright and `state` lands on LOCAL - decisive where it happens, diluted by a wide shot - by 0.0039 of frame. IT LANDED BELOW ITS OWN PREDICTION, 0.12% against 0.1694%, 0.71x - and this is the corpus's FIRST sub-prediction that is not a broken artifact. The rule earned by four prior cases is that below the floor means broken; three artifacts had landed under and all three were. So this was investigated rather than argued away, by diffing the two frames directly:   670 changed pixels, max delta 236, bbox 409 x 76 px   per bay: ghost 406 | sweep 71 | terminus 86 | formula 107 | none 0 The change is STRUCTURED, not noise, and it is the artifact's own argument in numbers: five answers to what a still can hold of a motion, and at a nudge `none` holds NOTHING - exactly zero changed pixels - while the rest betray the motion in proportion to the apparatus they carry. WHY THE RASTERISER OVER-PREDICTED, which is a fact about the instrument's domain and not about this artifact. Every corpus prediction until now UNDER-predicted (1.5x to 7.4x) because a Python rasteriser has one light, flat shading and no shadows, AO or antialiasing - it cannot see most of what separates two real renders. Here the subject is WIREFRAME - all edges, no solid faces - and the displacement at reach=nudge is on the order of a pixel. With no antialiasing the rasteriser snaps an edge to whole pixels and over-registers the move; Godot at MSAA 4x smears the same displacement into a gradient that falls under the diff threshold. The bias inverts precisely where the change is sub-pixel and the marks are one pixel wide. SO THE FLOOR RULE HAS A DOMAIN, now measured: it holds for changes larger than a few pixels, and inverts below that on edge-only subjects. A sub-prediction still means STOP AND INVESTIGATE; it no longer means broken on its own. THE AXIS IS THIN AND HONESTLY SO. 0.12% is under the 1.0% floor verify_batch was run at, and a nudge that moved more would not be a nudge. The reach axis is what carries the separation.
